rows.description: I look up to my mentor and feel eager to be like them. I learn from their wisdom, ask hard questions, and remember they are a person with flaws; blind hero worship leaves me without my own judgment.

rows.description: My mentor spent hours guiding me and I want to repay them. I thank them sincerely, apply what they taught, and pass it on to others; the best return is to grow and help another.

rows.description: I discover my mentor cut corners or is petty and feel let down. I keep the lessons that were true, hold them as human, and set boundaries if their conduct is harmful; I neither deny it nor discard everything they gave.

rows.description: My mentor uses me for free labour, credit, or personal errands under the name of guidance and I feel torn between loyalty and unfairness. I speak up, ask for fair learning and recognition, and leave if the pattern continues.

rows.description: My mentor seems threatened as I grow and starts to undercut or block me and I feel confused. I keep respecting what they taught, seek other guides, and do not shrink to protect their ego.

rows.description: A younger person looks up to me and I feel proud and a bit self-important. I share honestly, including failures, encourage their independence, and see mentoring as service and not a mirror for my ego.
